fields.label: GitHub Action YAML
fields.default:
# Copyright (c) 2026, Rokct Intelligence (pty) Ltd.
# For license information, please see license.txt
#
# Reviewable source of the workflow that `setup_github_workflow`
# (agent/frappe/src/roadmap/api.py) commits into a roadmap's source repository
# as `.github/workflows/rokct_pr_merged.yml`.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH, BUT IT IS NOT WHAT GETS INSTALLED.
# The body actually installed comes from `Roadmap Settings.github_action_yaml`,
# whose default lives in `doctype/roadmap_settings/roadmap_settings.json`. That
# stored copy is run through `str.format`, so in the stored copy every brace
# except the api_endpoint_url placeholder is doubled. The two must be kept in
# step; the pull request that introduced this file records the one-line
# transform that regenerates the stored default from this one.
#
# THIS IS THE SECOND OF TWO ROUTES, AND THE NARROWER ONE.
# The Protocol distributes the same workflow, to the same path, to every
# repository whose `remote.origin.url` is under `RokctAI/`: `initiate` copies
# each file in the Protocol's `workflows/.rok/` into the consumer's
# `.github/workflows/`. Inside the organisation that route wins, because it
# needs no per-repository step at all. This route exists for the case that one
# cannot serve: a roadmap whose `source_repository` is OUTSIDE the RokctAI
# organisation, where nothing copies the file in and the site has to commit it
# through the Contents API.
#
# The body below is therefore kept deliberately identical to the Protocol's
# copy at `workflows/.rok/rokct_pr_merged.yml`; two copies of one workflow
# drifting apart is the failure mode to avoid. The complete set of differences
# is this header and two edits, both marked DIFFERS FROM THE PROTOCOL COPY.
#
# Configuration resolves in this order, highest first:
#
#   ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT  repository Actions variable, then repository
#                           secret, then the organisation-level value of
#                           either. Falls back to the URL of the site that
#                           installed this file, templated in at install time.
#                           An in-org repository therefore inherits the org
#                           default and an out-of-org repository gets the
#                           hard-wired site URL, with no manual step in either.
#   ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET    OPTIONAL repository or organisation Actions secret
#                           - a dedicated HMAC key. When it is unset the
#                           signing key falls back to MONOREPO_PAT. An HMAC key
#                           is only a shared string, so either value serves;
#                           whichever is in force, the site's `Roadmap Settings
#                           > GitHub Action Secret` must hold that same value.
#                           The request body is always signed; nothing is ever
#                           sent unsigned. INSIDE the organisation MONOREPO_PAT
#                           is already inherited by every repository, so there
#                           is no per-repository step at all. OUTSIDE the
#                           organisation neither secret is inherited and a
#                           human must add ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET to the
#                           repository by hand - that is the case this route
#                           exists for.
#
# Because the endpoint always resolves - the templated fallback is never empty
# - the "no endpoint configured" branches of the first step cannot fire in this
# copy, and the live check is the missing-secret one. They are kept anyway so
# that the two copies stay one file with one shape.
#
# Known limitation: Actions withholds organisation and repository secrets from
# `pull_request` runs originating in a fork, so a merged fork pull request
# reaches the "not configured" branch and reports nothing. Pull requests from
# branches inside the repository are unaffected. Fixing it means moving to
# `pull_request_target`, which runs in the base repository's context with its
# secrets; that is deliberately not done here.

name: ROKCT roadmap - report merged pull request

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: read
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  report-merge:
    # `closed` fires for abandoned pull requests too. Only a merge closes a
    # roadmap feature, so everything below is gated on `merged`.
    if: github.event.pull_request.merged == true
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Runs before any API call so a repository with no roadmap spends one
      # step and stops, rather than querying GitHub for an answer it will
      # throw away.
      - name: Check whether this repository has a roadmap callback configured
        id: config
        env:
          # DIFFERS FROM THE PROTOCOL COPY: the templated fallback, so a
          # repository outside the organisation - which inherits no org
          # variable - still reaches the site that installed this file.
          ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT: >-
            ${{{{ vars.ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT || secrets.ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT || '{api_endpoint_url}' }}}}
          ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET: ${{{{ secrets.ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET }}}}
          # The key actually used to sign. An HMAC key is only a shared
          # string, so the org-wide MONOREPO_PAT serves as one and nothing new
          # has to be created; a dedicated ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET still wins
          # where one exists. Kept separate from ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET above so
          # that the checks below can still tell "somebody configured a
          # roadmap here" from "this repository merely inherits the org PAT".
          ROKCT_ROADMAP_SIGNING_KEY: >-
            ${{{{ secrets.ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET || secrets.MONOREPO_PAT }}}}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          if [ -z "${{ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT:-}}" ] && [ -z "${{ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET:-}}" ]; then
            echo "No ROKCT roadmap callback configured for this repository; nothing to report."
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          # Half-configured is a mistake worth surfacing, but not worth
          # failing a merged pull request over: the merge already happened and
          # this job only reports it.
          if [ -z "${{ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT:-}}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET is set but ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT is not; skipping the roadmap callback."
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          if [ -z "${{ROKCT_ROADMAP_SIGNING_KEY:-}}" ]; then
            # DIFFERS FROM THE PROTOCOL COPY: names where the value comes
            # from, which only the installing site knows.
            echo "::warning::ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT is set but no signing key is available - neither ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET nor MONOREPO_PAT is set; skipping the roadmap callback rather than sending an unsigned request. Add an Actions secret named ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET holding the value of the ROKCT site's Roadmap Settings > GitHub Action Secret."
            echo "configured=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          echo "configured=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Resolve the issue this pull request closes
        id: issue
        if: steps.config.outputs.configured == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{{{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}}}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{{{ github.event.pull_request.number }}}}
          PR_BODY: ${{{{ github.event.pull_request.body }}}}
          REPO_OWNER: ${{{{ github.repository_owner }}}}
          REPO_NAME: ${{{{ github.event.repository.name }}}}
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail

          # Primary: GitHub's own linked-issue graph. `closingIssuesReferences`
          # is populated both by closing keywords in the pull request body and
          # by issues linked by hand from the Development sidebar, and it
          # already understands every keyword spelling GitHub accepts.
          issue_number="$(
            gh api graphql \
              -f query='query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $pr: Int!) {{ repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {{ pullRequest(number: $pr) {{ closingIssuesReferences(first: 10) {{ nodes {{ number }} }} }} }} }}' \
              -f owner="$REPO_OWNER" \
              -f name="$REPO_NAME" \
              -F pr="$PR_NUMBER" \
              --jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.closingIssuesReferences.nodes[].number] | first // empty'
          )" || issue_number=""

          # Fallback: read the closing keyword straight out of the body, for
          # repositories where the GITHUB_TOKEN cannot reach the GraphQL API.
          if [ -z "$issue_number" ]; then
            issue_number="$(
              printf '%s' "$PR_BODY" \
                | grep -oiE '\b(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)[[:space:]]+#[0-9]+' \
                | grep -oE '[0-9]+' \
                | head -n 1
            )" || issue_number=""
          fi

          case "$issue_number" in
            "" | *[!0-9]*)
              echo "No closing issue reference on pull request #${{PR_NUMBER}}; nothing to report."
              echo "found=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
              ;;
          esac

          echo "Pull request #${{PR_NUMBER}} closes issue #${{issue_number}}."
          echo "found=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "number=${{issue_number}}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Report the merge to the ROKCT roadmap
        if: steps.config.outputs.configured == 'true' && steps.issue.outputs.found == 'true'
        env:
          # DIFFERS FROM THE PROTOCOL COPY: the templated fallback, so a
          # repository outside the organisation - which inherits no org
          # variable - still reaches the site that installed this file.
          ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT: >-
            ${{{{ vars.ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT || secrets.ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT || '{api_endpoint_url}' }}}}
          ROKCT_ROADMAP_SIGNING_KEY: >-
            ${{{{ secrets.ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET || secrets.MONOREPO_PAT }}}}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{{{ steps.issue.outputs.number }}}}
          PR_URL: ${{{{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}}}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # Build the body once and sign exactly the bytes that get sent.
          # `jq -c` emits no trailing newline once the command substitution has
          # stripped it, `printf '%s'` adds none, and `--data-binary @-` sends
          # stdin verbatim -- so the digest below is taken over the identical
          # byte sequence the receiver hashes as `frappe.request.data`.
          body="$(
            jq -cn \
              --argjson issue_number "$ISSUE_NUMBER" \
              --arg pull_request_url "$PR_URL" \
              '{{issue_number: $issue_number, pull_request_url: $pull_request_url}}'
          )"

          signature="$(
            printf '%s' "$body" \
              | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$ROKCT_ROADMAP_SIGNING_KEY" \
              | awk '{{print $NF}}'
          )"

          printf '%s' "$body" | curl \
            --silent --show-error --fail-with-body \
            --request POST "$ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT" \
            --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            --header "X-Hub-Signature-256: sha256=${{signature}}" \
            --data-binary @-
fields.description: Committed to a roadmap's source repository as .github/workflows/rokct_pr_merged.yml, for roadmaps whose source repository is outside the RokctAI organisation. Inside the organisation the Protocol already distributes the same file to the same path on every initiate run, so setup_github_workflow finds it present and only marks the roadmap Linked. The default is the workflow kept at agent/frappe/src/roadmap/rokct_pr_merged.yml; edit that file and regenerate this default rather than diverging. {api_endpoint_url} is substituted with this site's callback URL at install time, so every other brace must stay doubled. The installed workflow reads ROKCT_ROADMAP_ENDPOINT and ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET from Actions configuration and falls back to the templated URL. The signing key is ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET when set, otherwise MONOREPO_PAT, which every repository in the organisation already inherits - so an in-org repository needs no secret step at all, and only an outside-the-org repository needs ROKCT_ROADMAP_SECRET added by hand. Whichever key is in force, the GitHub Action Secret field below must hold that same value.
